claim: Non-EU sellers pay 24% on the gain, EU/EEA 19% (TL;DR, body, table, FAQ, schema)
evidence: Art. 25.1.f.3 TRLIRNR: 19 por ciento for 'Ganancias patrimoniales que se pongan de manifiesto con ocasion de transmisiones de elementos patrimoniales', applies to every non-resident. 24% (art. 25.1.a) is the general rate for other income.
action: Corrected to 19% for all non-residents everywhere; UK FAQ rewritten; Brexit 24% explained for rents via AEAT page

claim: Buyer withholds 3% (art. 25.2) and pays via Modelo 211 within one month
verdict: OK (one month from the transfer date, not from the notarial deed)
evidence: Art. 25.2: 'el adquirente estara obligado a retener e ingresar el 3 por ciento ... de la contraprestacion acordada, en concepto de pago a cuenta'. Orden EHA/3316/2010 art. 8.5: plazo de un mes a partir de la fecha de la transmision; art. 8.4: buyer gives the seller a copy.
action: Wording changed to one month from the transfer date; verbatim quote of 25.2 added

claim: Modelo 210 filed within four months of the sale; missing it loses the refund
evidence: Art. 5.a Orden EHA/3316/2010 (consolidated, in force 24 June 2026, wording unchanged by HAC/623/2026): 'en el plazo de tres meses una vez transcurrido el plazo de un mes desde la fecha de la transmision', whatever the result. No loss of refund stated.
action: Rewritten as three-month period opening after one month; refund-loss claim removed

evidence: AEAT note on HAC/623/2026 covers rents and imputed income only; consolidated art. 5.a text is identical in the 2011, 2024 and 2026 versions.

claim: AEAT refunds the excess retention typically within six to twelve months
evidence: AEAT says 'Si la retencion es superior a la cuota tributaria, se podra obtener la devolucion del exceso'. No period stated.

claim: Plusvalia due within 30 working days; taxpayer may choose the lower of two methods
evidence: TRLRHL art. 110.2.a: treinta dias habiles for inter vivos acts; art. 110.4 optional self-assessment; art. 107.5: real increase is the base if lower, art. 104.5 no tax if no increase; art. 106.2: buyer is substitute taxpayer when the seller is a non-resident individual; RDL 26/2021 after STC 182/2021.

claim: Non-resident buyers 20% of housing transactions in 2025 (Registrars); complete files complete in 30 to 45 days; notary and registry fees 0.5% to 1%; nota simple within 30 days
evidence: No source in the post; none found

claim: Energy certificate and IBI receipts are legal preconditions to any sale
evidence: RD 390/2021 art. 17.2: a copy of the registered certificate and label is annexed to the sale contract. No source makes IBI receipts a precondition.
action: Energy certificate sentence rewritten; IBI precondition removed

evidence: LPH art. 9.1.e: without the debt certificate the notary cannot authorise the deed unless the buyer expressly waives it; secretary issues it within seven calendar days.

claim: Overlooking Modelo 720 for Spanish accounts remaining after the sale
evidence: Modelo 720 reports assets abroad of Spanish tax residents, not Spanish accounts of non-residents (see 15116).
action: Replaced by a sentence on residents and a link to 15116

claim: 183 days makes you tax resident; filing as non-resident triggers penalties and interest
evidence: LIRPF art. 9.1: more than 183 days in the calendar year or main base of economic interests in Spain; treaty tie-breakers (UK-Spain 2013, US-Spain 1990 art. 4). Penalty sentence unsourced.

claim: Non-residents cannot offset losses across income categories
evidence: TRLIRNR art. 15.1: tributan de forma separada por cada devengo, sin que sea posible compensacion alguna

claim: Allowable expenses on sale include energy certificate cost and legal fees
evidence: LIRPF art. 35.2: gastos y tributos inherentes a la transmision satisfechos por el transmitente; which costs qualify is case specific.
action: Reworded to the article and the agent commission example, CTA

claim: Brexit: reinvestment exemption for main home not available to UK residents
evidence: AEAT page on Brexit consequences lists the exemption among those that stop applying; 19% general rate stops, 24% applies to rents etc.
